claims.text: SOLID is an acronym for five design principles, one per letter; the S is the Single Responsibility Principle.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry solid; standard definition in software design literature

claims.text: The Single Responsibility Principle states that a class should have only one reason to change.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry srp; standard formulation in software design literature

claims.text: PlaceOrderSplit has Place plus four private static methods: FirstProblemWith (input checks), TotalWithShippingVnd (total plus shipping fee), Save and Notify (each a Console.WriteLine).
The shipping fee threshold 2_000_000 is in TotalWithShippingVnd; a new input check (e.g. at most 20 order lines) would go in FirstProblemWith; Save and Notify only print lines.
PlaceOrderSplit.cs is under 40 lines at stage-0 (38 lines).

Try-it requests map to one method each: id above 1,000,000 -> FirstProblemWith; loyal customers never pay shipping -> TotalWithShippingVnd (has customerIsLoyal); print date -> Save; thank-you text -> Notify.
SRP asks for one class per reason to change (validator, pricer, order saver, notifier); Place, running the steps in order, can remain as all of PlaceOrderSplit and changes only when the steps change.
claims.source_hint: outline items 2 and 4; follows from the SRP definition

claims.text: Asking who would request a change is a practical way to spot distinct reasons to change.

self_check.notes: Outline item 4 said 'repository', a term taught later; outline changed to 'order saver'. Classes described as ideas only, per depth_notes. Round 1: dropped untaught OCP/LSP/ISP/DIP letters, Try-it uses new requests (not answered in section 5), Place's remaining role stated.
